content:
lucas: Quick copy review for the 'Optimize' suggestion tooltip that shows next to quantization recommendations. Current tooltip: `Use 4-bit for lower cost` 12 feels terse and a bit vague about quality impact.
priya: Yep. Users ask whether accuracy will change, if it's safe for their model, and what the tradeoffs are. Tooltip needs to be concise but actionable.
dave: Also accessibility: tooltips need accessible names and keyboard focus. For screen readers we should ensure there's a companion help text in the panel.
kim: Copy constraints: tooltip must be under ~120 chars. We can offer a short line + link to an expanded panel or patternfly popover. Proposed variants:\n\nA) Short (informal): "Switch to 4-bit quantization to lower cost. May slightly change output quality."
B) Neutral (recommended): "Try 4-bit quantization to reduce inference cost. Minimal quality differences for most prompts; test before deploying."
C) Prescriptive (enterprise): "4-bit quantization reduces cost and memory. Expected small differences in output. Use for non-critical workloads or run a canary rollout."

design-bot: [automated] Current tooltip=`Use 4-bit for lower cost` severity=info code=OPT_SUGGEST_QUANT retention=10s
priya: I like B but tweak 'test before deploying' -> 'test with a representative prompt set'. Also change 'most prompts' -> 'most workloads' (broader).
lucas: Can we show an inline microcopy for estimated impact like "~1-3% quality delta" ? I know we don't have exact metrics yet. If we can't, show a link "See benchmark" which opens an anchored modal with numbers.
dave: For keyboard users, tooltip shouldn't disappear on hover leave if focused. Add an ARIA-describedby ID linking tooltip to the 'Optimize' card. SR text: "Recommendation: Try 4-bit quantization to reduce cost. Expected small output differences; test with representative prompts. Press Enter to open details."
kim: Tones: keep neutral, avoid 'downgrade' or 'lossy'. Use 'smaller memory footprint' / 'lower cost'. Also include a clear CTA when relevant: "Preview impact" opens a small eval runner.
priya: Variants with CTAs (short + CTA):
1) "Try 4-bit quantization to lower inference cost. Test with representative prompts. Preview impact."
2) "4-bit quantization reduces memory and cost. Expected small differences for many workloads. Run a quick preview."

lucas: UX micro-interaction: when user clicks 'Preview impact', show a lightweight A/B diff using a sample prompt with a short explanation line: "This preview compares your current model vs 4-bit variant on a representative prompt." Keep the tooltip CTAs conservative to avoid surprise.
dave: Accessibility nit: avoid auto-opening the preview on click without confirmation; ensure dialog is keyboard-trappable and announced. Tooltip should not rely solely on color to indicate risk.
kim: Copy for the anchored modal header: "Quantization: 4-bit (cost vs. quality)" Body intro: "4-bit quantization reduces memory use and inference cost. Below are benchmark samples — run them against your prompts to see differences." Buttons: primary="Run preview" secondary="Close"
priya: Also propose telemetry: track clicks on 'Preview impact' and whether preview led to rollout. Add label `opt_suggest_quant_preview_clicked`.
dave: Implementation ask: show the suggestion only when model architecture is compatible; otherwise hide CTA and change tooltip to "Not compatible with this model". Copy for that state: "Quantization not supported for this model architecture."
lucas: Action items: 1) Priya will lock in variant B with phrasing edits and SR text. 2) Kim will update the tooltip microcopy in the mock and add the 'Preview impact' CTA. 3) Dave will add a11y checklist for tooltip/focus/announcements. 4) I'll sync with infra about adding benchmark links and approximate deltas when available.
kim: Final proposed tooltip (concise, SR-friendly): "Try 4-bit quantization to reduce inference cost. Expected small output differences for many workloads. Test with representative prompts. Preview impact." SR version (no punctuation parens): "Recommendation try four-bit quantization to reduce inference cost expected small output differences for many workloads test with representative prompts preview impact"
priya: Approved pending copy in PR and a screenshot. :thumbsup:
